subject: DeltaWorks on‑prem headroom alignment and carveout plan
messages:
From: Sandeep Reddy <sandeep.reddy@deltaworks.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marie Chen <marie.chen@deltaworks.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Oct 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial ask — carveout throughput targets and fallback behavior

Hi Marissa,

Quick note from our infra team: we're preparing the on‑prem carveout (phase 1) and need to lock down the throughput headroom and fallback policies before procurement signs off. High level context: DeltaWorks plans to route ~60k inference requests/day initially, with spiky daily peaks up to 10x for promo traffic. Typical request payloads are short (average 120 tokens output) but we have a small percentage (~5%) of long‑form generation (1k+ tokens).

Questions we need answered to finalize sizing and networking:
- Recommended sustained QPS target and burst headroom per reserved pool (single AZ).
- Concurrency and KV‑cache warmup strategy for mixed short/long requests.
- Egress bandwidth assumptions and NIC oversubscription guidance.
- Failure/fallback model: what model variants to keep as cheap fallbacks and how that impacts throughput commitments.

Attaching our observed QPS profile for last 30 days (deltaworks_qps_profile_oct2025.csv). Can your team propose a conservative carveout plan and a short ops checklist we can take to procurement?

Thanks,
Sandeep
Engineering Ops — DeltaWorks

Subject: Re: Initial ask — carveout throughput targets and fallback behavior

Sandeep — thanks for the clear context and the QPS CSV. We can run a conservative carveout proposal for Phase 1 this week. High level notes up front so you can share with procurement:

1) Sustained target: recommend reserving for 300 QPS sustained across the pool to cover baseline and usual peaks. For your math: 300 QPS ≈ 25.9M tokens/day at 120 tokens/request (leaves capacity for long requests via headroom).
2) Burst headroom: provision 3x burst (~900 QPS) with an autoscale policy that permits short 120s windows for bursts. This keeps latency SLOs while avoiding full overprovisioning.
3) Concurrency: target 2.5 average in‑flight requests per GPU slot for mixed short workloads; use per‑tenant admission control to prioritize short jobs when the queue is deep.
4) KV cache warmup: reserve a small warm pool (10% of nodes) pinned to hot tenants; treat long‑form requests with conservative cache reuse and prefetch hints from your app layer.
5) Egress: assume 10 Gbps per 8‑GPU tile for mixed traffic with NIC oversub up to 1.6x during short spikes; recommend 25% headroom in your rack egress budgeting.
6) Fallback strategy: maintain a quantized / smaller model variant as the default fallback (e.g., 4‑bit quant) and a medium variant for degraded mode. We can cap the fallback throughput in policy to preserve higher‑quality serving for critical routes.

I'll loop in Irene and Jonas for a short carveout topology and a proposed tile tiling plan. Attaching a quick sketch (proposed‑carveout‑tiling‑v1.pdf).

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial ask — carveout throughput targets and fallback behavior

Thanks team — I dug into the CSV and ran a quick projection. A few concrete operational knobs and risks to flag:

- Admission control thresholds: set soft admission at 85% tile utilization and hard admission at 95% to avoid queue tails. Soft admission should trigger rapid cache eviction and short‑job prioritization.
- Warm pool sizing: 10% reserved nodes for cache warm = good starting point; for your traffic we recommend running a 72‑hour warmup simulation before go‑live to validate cache hit ratio.
- Long request mitigation: route long‑form generation to dedicated lanes that cap concurrency to 1 per GPU to bound latency variance and reduce KV pressure on short lanes.
- Networking: for single AZ on‑prem, recommend redundant 25Gbps uplinks with LACP across aggregation switches. Egress shaping should apply per‑tenant burst buckets.
- Cost/throughput trade: fallback model reduces tokens/sec by ~40% but multiplies QPS headroom by ~2.5x — useful during big promos.

Next steps I propose:
1) Infra sketch + tiling plan (Jonas).
2) Admission + warmup runbook draft (Karthik).
3) Short ops checklist for procurement (Marissa).

Irene
Senior SRE — Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Initial ask — carveout throughput targets and fallback behavior

Attaching tiling sketches and a short rationale. Key decisions:
- 8‑GPU tiles (A100 class) with 3 tiles per rack for Phase 1; each tile sized for ~100 sustained QPS of short requests when using the standard model. That aligns with Marissa's 300 QPS baseline across pool.
- Network: keep per‑tile NICs in active/backup LACP pairs; use host eBPF policing to enforce per‑tenant egress buckets before hardware queues.
- Admission: implement a two‑tier queue: short queue (fast path) and long queue (bounded concurrency). Fast path has preemptible tokens for microbursts.

Notes on failure modes: If a tile loses NVLink connectivity (rare), autoscaler should drain remaining requests to fallback tiles and enable fallback model with a 60s warm grace period. We also include an emergency flat‑rate throttle to protect datastore/backing services.

This is very helpful — thanks. Two quick clarifications from procurement and networking:
1) Procurement asked for a conservative egress budget line item. Can you convert the 10 Gbps per 8‑GPU tile assumption into an expected daily GiB egress estimate for Phase 1 (300 QPS sustained, 10% long requests at 1k tokens each)?
2) Networking wants specific NIC oversub recommended limits (we have options for 1.2x, 1.6x, 2.0x). Which would you pick for single‑AZ with redundant 25Gbps uplinks?

Also, can you place the draft ops checklist somewhere we can reference from our procurement doc?

Appreciate the quick turnaround — looking to close this week.

Sandeep

Sandeep — answers inline below and linking the short ops checklist to your drive link (see related_links).

1) Egress estimate (daily):
   - Baseline (300 QPS sustained, 120 output tokens/request average, ~1.6 bytes/token compressed): ~5.0 GiB/day egress for typical short requests.
   - Long requests (10% of traffic → 30 QPS at 1,000 tokens): ~4.0 GiB/day.
   - Total conservative estimate: ~9.5 GiB/day (round up to 12 GiB/day to allow protocol overhead and logs).

2) NIC oversubscription recommendation: pick 1.6x for single‑AZ with redundant 25Gbps uplinks. Rationale: balances cost and short‑burst absorption; 2.0x increases contention risk for multi‑tenant noisy neighbors, 1.2x is too conservative vs your burst profile.

We dropped the ops checklist into the shared Drive under: https://drive.redwood/reports/deltaworks-capacity-runway (see related_links). The checklist includes: pre‑deploy warmup simulation, 72‑hour KV cache validation, canary rollout steps, telemetry dashboard links, and rollback triggers.

If procurement needs a line that maps tiles→GiB/day per tile, say: 8‑GPU tile = 3.5 GiB/day (typical mixed mix) — multiply by 3 tiles for Phase 1 equals ~10.5 GiB/day.

Happy to jump on a 30m call if you want to lock language for the procurement SOW.

Best,
Marissa
Director, Customer Solutions — Redwood Inference
